verdict.headline: Brent closes below $85 for first time; chip rout extends with AMD −9% as FOMC looms
verdict.label: Oil regime takes a concrete step toward clearance; semiconductors in free fall — FOMC and Mag-7 earnings tomorrow decide the week
verdict.rationale_short: Tuesday closed with a split regime verdict: Brent crude settled at $84.09, falling below the $85 formal breach trigger for the first time since the Iran conflict began, while WTI fell to $79.26, just $0.26 above its own $79 clearance level. Simultaneously the semiconductor rout deepened — AMD fell 8.85%, Micron fell 8.4%, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 4.35% for a fourth consecutive session — while NVDA unexpectedly recovered to $197.34 (+0.4%) as institutional money narrowed the AI chip trade to the single name with the most irreplaceable position in the ecosystem. The Dow gained 1.03% on industrials and consumer earnings; AAPL hit a new all-time closing high at $340.08. Wednesday brings the year's most concentrated information window: FOMC rate decision at 2pm ET (expected hold; Warsh's language on September is the true binary), followed by META Q2 and MSFT Q4 FY26 AH where FY27 capex guidance against AI ROI trajectory is the structural question that resolves — or extends — the two-week AI infrastructure selloff.

dont_buy.reason: AMD's −8.85% Tuesday decline — from $512 Monday to ~$467 — is driven by a structural repricing of the AI hyperscaler capex ROI thesis, not a technical selloff. The CXMT Chinese memory competition, NVDA circular financing concern (which reprices overall AI capex reliability), and the MSFT Azure guidance binary on Wednesday are three unresolved inputs that all affect AMD's MI400 hyperscaler win thesis. Bottom-fishing into Wednesday's FOMC + MSFT earnings binary is position-size doubling on the wrong side of the information curve.
dont_buy.better_entry: Post-FOMC Wednesday AND post-MSFT Azure guidance: if Azure confirms >42% growth with credible AI monetization ROI AND FOMC is explicitly dovish, AMD entry at $460–470 with stop at $440 is defensible. If MSFT capex guidance follows the GOOGL −7% template, AMD faces another leg down toward $420–430.

dont_buy.reason: SMH fell >3% on Tuesday for a fourth consecutive session; the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index has declined 4.35% in a single day. The sector faces three simultaneous headwinds entering Wednesday: (1) FOMC language on September could re-anchor hawkish trajectory that impairs AI capex spending; (2) MSFT Azure guidance is AMD/NVDA's most important Q3 demand signal; (3) META AI ad ROI vs. $40B+ AI capex spend determines whether AI infrastructure spend is commercially justified. Adding SMH/SOXX before all three clear is fighting three unresolved binaries without an edge.
dont_buy.better_entry: Post-FOMC Wednesday close and post-META/MSFT AH. If FOMC dovish AND MSFT Azure >42% AND META operating margin holds above 40%, re-entry in SMH/SOXX at Wednesday's close with stop at Tuesday's close price.

trade_setups.asset: FOMC rates binary (TBT long / TLT pair)
trade_setups.thesis: Tomorrow's FOMC statement (2pm ET, Warsh press conference 2:30pm) is the year's single highest-information event for rates. Brent clearing $85 today weakens the hawkish case; Warsh inherits: first Brent close below $85 since the conflict began (reduces near-term inflation embedding), Durable Goods +0.3% vs. +2.5% expected (soft capex), 30Y at 5.10% (still above 5.00% trigger), and September hike probability still near the 70% formal threshold. The pair captures both outcomes without directional bet: dovish language (September de-emphasized) → TLT long, upgrade clock potentially starts; hawkish language (September explicitly live, tariff CPI embedding acknowledged) → TBT long, 30Y tests 5.20%, SPX tests 7,380.
trade_setups.entry: Build equal-weight TBT long / TLT long pair into Tuesday's close — 16 hours before the decision. Let FOMC July 29 2pm decide which leg converts to directional. Close the losing leg within 30 minutes of the 2pm statement. Hold the winner for 2–3 weeks through August CPI (est. Aug 13).
trade_setups.invalidation: FOMC statement is fully ambiguous — acknowledges both inflation risk and soft growth without explicitly signaling September either way. 10Y holds 4.64% ±2bps post-statement. Flatten both legs within 60 minutes.
trade_setups.horizon: Through FOMC July 29; convert survivor to August CPI hold

Both required simultaneously to flip bullish on AMD. Single condition alone is insufficient — cover half-position on one, full cover on both.

bear_case: Counter-argument: Brent clearing $85 today may be premature regime credit — the Iran ceasefire is still a verbal mutual pause with no written terms, no Hormuz reopening protocol, and no Iranian concession on nuclear enrichment. A single confrontation at sea or a failed round of Oman-mediated talks could send Brent back above $90 within 24 hours, resetting the clearance to zero. NVDA's +0.4% recovery and AMD's −8.85% decline could reflect positioning ahead of a short-squeeze on NVDA if MSFT Azure beats Thursday — in which case tomorrow's tape could be the opposite of today's, with NVDA spiking and AMD recovering on sector relief. The FOMC's language tomorrow could explicitly acknowledge that September is live (Warsh inherits a 30Y above 5.00% and tariffs on 99.4% of imports still embedding), which would re-anchor the hawkish case even with Brent below $85. If the 30Y breaks 5.20% on a hawkish hold, SPX tests 7,380 in the same session that META and MSFT report — and if either company follows GOOGL's −7% capex-without-ROI template, the combination triggers a cascade from 7,428 toward 7,250. Bear case invalidation: formal written Iran-US ceasefire terms announced before Wednesday's open, or FOMC explicitly de-emphasizes September AND both META/MSFT demonstrate improving AI capex ROI QoQ. If SPX reclaims 7,480 on the post-FOMC close Wednesday, the call is wrong.
